name: Sagebrush shrubland
notes: Grey-green big sagebrush 1-2 m dominates with bunchgrasses between shrubs; pinyon and juniper only on slopes; Great Basin and Columbia Plateau of the western USA.

canopy.source: Pinus monophylla, Great Basin pinyon-juniper woodland, 5-12 m — USDA PLANTS

traits.native_range: Pinus monophylla, Great Basin pinyon-juniper woodland, 5-12 m — USDA PLANTS
traits.leaf_shape: needles or scale leaves, evergreen (larch deciduous)
traits.trunk: single straight trunk, whorled branches, conical crown
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings, usually from seeds cached by jays under shrubs, have 7-9 cotyledons and bluish primary needles, then unique single, round, stiff, sharp grey-green needles (the only pine with one needle per bundle). Young trees are compact, bluish cones; old ones become rounded, flat-topped and often multi-stemmed.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Pinus monophylla: a dominant tree takes ~60 years to reach 2 m and ~150 to reach 8.5 m (about 5 cm/yr); first cones ~35 yrs, good crops from 75-100, peak at 160-200; not shade tolerant; dominants often 400 years, some 800-1,000

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS (strobili late spring-early summer, pollen shed by mid-June; three-season cone cycle, ripe seed about 26 months after the buds form; cones 3.5-5.5 cm, thick-scaled, open Sep-Nov; masting every 2-3 years); its large wingless nuts were a Great Basin staple

canopy.silhouette: squat rounded juniper, shreddy grey trunk

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings have needle-like juvenile leaves 5-10 mm long, making a soft, prickly little blue-green cone; scale leaves take over within a few years. Growth is very slow (often only a few cm a year) and seedlings usually establish under a nurse shrub, becoming after decades a rounded, bushy, often multi-trunked tree with shreddy grey bark.
growth.source: USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual (J. osteosperma: flowers Mar-Apr, cones ripen in 2nd year, reddish-brown with bloom, persist ~2 yr, 1-2 seeds, good crops about every 2 yr, bears from 10-20 yr); Wikipedia (3-6 m, cones 8-13 mm maturing in ~18 months, juvenile needles 5-10 mm). Growth rate and longevity estimated.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (cones 8-13 mm, blue-brown with whitish waxy bloom, mature in ~18 months, pollen shed early spring; eaten and dispersed by jackrabbits, coyotes, solitaires); USDA WPSM (reddish-brown ripe cones persist ~2 yr). Set, crop and rot estimated.

shrub.name: Antelope bitterbrush
shrub.source: Purshia tridentata, Great Basin and intermountain west, browse shrub 0.6-3 m, cream flowers — USDA PLANTS

traits.native_range: Purshia tridentata, Great Basin and intermountain west, browse shrub 0
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings usually come up in tight clumps of 5-30 from a forgotten rodent seed cache. Each has two small oval cotyledons, then tiny wedge-shaped leaves with three teeth at the tip, grey-green above and woolly-white below, on one thin stem. The taproot races ahead while the top grows slowly; after some years it branches into a stiff, twiggy, rounded grey-green shrub.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Purshia tridentata (seed needs 4-6 wk chilling at 2 C; seed-bearing at 8-10 yr; plants of 115 and 128 yr; usually 0.9-1.2 m, up to 4.5 m; shade intolerant; natural regeneration mostly from rodent caches); Wikipedia (1-5 m; leaves 5-20 mm, 3-5-lobed)

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS Purshia tridentata (flowers early spring to Jul; insect-pollinated, wind possible in dense stands; highly self-incompatible; achenes 3-13 mm ripen Jul-Sep and fall beneath the shrub when dry, then rodents cache them); Wikipedia (5 pale yellow petals 6-8 mm); fruit set, crop and decay estimated

shrub.name: Big sagebrush
shrub.source: Artemisia tridentata, dominant Great Basin shrub, grey-green aromatic 0.6-2.5 m — USDA PLANTS

traits.native_range: Artemisia tridentata, dominant Great Basin shrub, grey-green aromatic 0
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: two small round cotyledons, then narrow, entire, silvery-hairy leaves; the wedge-shaped leaves with three blunt teeth at the tip come a few weeks later. It stays a single-stemmed silver sprig for a year or two while its roots race down, then branches into a rounded, aromatic, silver-grey bush with a short twisted trunk and shreddy bark.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Artemisia tridentata subsp. tridentata: germination in 2-3 days at all test temperatures, in late fall/winter or after snowmelt; plants 2-3 yr old can bear viable seed; commonly 40-50 yr, some over 100 yr; 1-2 m, up to 5 m. Height-age curve and shade class estimated.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS basin big sagebrush: flowers late Aug-Oct; seed ripens and disperses Oct-Dec over ~8 weeks, ~90% within 9 m; self- or wind-pollinated; more prolific than Wyoming big sagebrush. Tiny heads of a few florets in leafy panicles; fruit set and crop estimated.

shrub.silhouette: bright green spiny shrub with white stems

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling with 2 long, narrow, fleshy cotyledons and a coiled embryo that uncoils fast; first leaves bright green, fleshy and cylindrical (1-4 cm) like the adult's. Grows slowly into a stiff, rigid, much-branched spiny shrub with pale bark; after 12 years only about 0.7 m tall on dry sites. Resprouts from the root crown.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Sarcobatus vermiculatus (transplants 0.73 m tall after 12 yr; to 3 m; vigorous crown sprouting); USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual Sarcobatus (67-91% germination in 2-10 days at 10 C); lifespan estimated from its slow growth

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS and Woody Plant Seed Manual Sarcobatus (monoecious, wind-pollinated; male flowers in small cone-like spikes at twig tips, female flowers single in leaf axils; tan winged utricles 4-5 mm, 1 cm across the wing, mature late Sep-Nov, a few hang until next summer)

shrub.name: Rubber rabbitbrush
shrub.source: Ericameria nauseosa, western N America sagebrush steppe, yellow autumn flowers, 0.6-2 m — USDA PLANTS

traits.native_range: Ericameria nauseosa, western N America sagebrush steppe, yellow autumn flowers, 0
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

shrub.silhouette: grey-green rounded shrub, gold flower top

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling with two small oval cotyledons, then thread-like grey-green leaves on white-felted stems while the root races down. By year 2 it is a small rounded bush of many erect, flexible, whitish-woolly green stems from the base, already topped with yellow flower clusters; full grown in about 4 years. Resprouts from stem buds after fire.
growth.source: USDA FEIS species review (Ericameria nauseosa): germination 5-20 days without stratification (T50 5-96 days by seed source); plants 'full grown' within 4 years (Stanton); post-fire epicormic sprouting. Lifespan estimated.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS (flowering Jul-Oct by elevation; seed ripe late Sep-Nov; plumed achenes wind-dispersed up to ~150 m; good crops every 1-2 yr, fruit fill variable; no persistent seed bank). Head size, heads per cluster, crop and rot estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds need a winter of chilling and sprout in spring. Epigeal seedling with two narrow cotyledons and small, round-oval, grey scurfy leaves; it grows slowly into a compact, rounded, grey-green shrublet whose older twigs harden into short spines. Seedlings survive best beside an established shrub.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Atriplex confertifolia (chilling needed, fungal breakdown of bracteoles, relatively short-lived, seedlings survive best near adults); Woody Plant Seed Manual (rarely germinable without chilling); growth rate and ages estimated.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS (flowers late Mar-mid Jun, dioecious, wind-pollinated, utricles in 2 round bracts 4-12 mm, mature ~25 weeks after flowering, persist through winter); Woody Plant Seed Manual (65-277 thousand fruits/kg); PFAF (seed eaten as mush); crop estimated.

traits.native_range: Balsamorhiza sagittata, sagebrush steppe forb with yellow sunflower heads, 20-60 cm — USDA PLANTS
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

ground.silhouette: silvery arrow leaves under big yellow daisies

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds need a long cold, wet winter and sprout right after snowmelt with two oval cotyledons. For years the plant is a small rosette of a few narrow, heart-based, silvery-hairy leaves while a taproot plunges deep; only after 3-8 years does it build the big clump of arrowhead-shaped, silver-woolly leaves and golden sunflower heads.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Balsamorhiza sagittata (12 weeks cold stratification, germinates at 0-10 C, weak seedling vigour, first flowering 3-4 yr on good sites and 7-8 yr on dry sites, long-lived, taproot to 2.7 m); lifespan figures estimated.

ground.name: Bluebunch wheatgrass
ground.source: Pseudoroegneria spicata, dominant bunchgrass of the sagebrush steppe, 0.4-1 m — USDA PLANTS

traits.native_range: Pseudoroegneria spicata, dominant bunchgrass of the sagebrush steppe, 0
traits.leaf_shape: narrow grass blades in a dense tussock
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds germinate with the autumn rains (or in spring) into a weak, slow-growing tuft of a few flat, blue-green blades whose roots grow more slowly than crested wheatgrass. Over several years tillers build a dense, erect bunch 30-100 cm tall with slender spikes of widely spaced spikelets (often with spreading awns), turning straw-coloured after seed-set in midsummer.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Pseudoroegneria spicata (facultative autumn germinator; poor establishment, weak seedlings; central Utah: growth from early April, flower stalks late May, full flower late June, seed ripe mid-July; 30-100 cm; roots to 1.4-2 m; light shade to open sites). Bunch size-age, first seed and lifespan estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: A fine thread-like first leaf, then a small tuft of very narrow, rolled, blue-green leaves. Tillers multiply each year into a dense round bunch 15-25 cm tall with basal leaves more than half the culm length. Establishment from seed is slow and episodic, but once established it is a long-lived bunchgrass.
growth.source: USDA FEIS species review (after-ripening dormancy, episodic establishment, long-lived bunchgrass with dense tufts 15-25 cm); USDA NRCS Plant Guide/Idaho PMC (weak seedling vigour, stands need 2-3 yr, little seed in yr 2 and full seed in yr 3; cited by an earlier research pass). Lifespan estimated.

ground.silhouette: airy bunchgrass with open lacy seed heads

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds are hard and often dormant for a year or more; seedlings appear mainly in cool, wet springs. The seedling is a single thin tiller with rolled, wiry, blue-green leaves above a fast, deep root; it slowly tillers into a small dense bunch and usually flowers from its second year, with airy, open panicles of plump black seeds on zigzag stalks.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Achnatherum hymenoides (seed dormancy, stratification in some ecotypes, 20 C optimum; seedling pulses follow wet Aprils; growth starts early Apr, seed ripe early Jul in Idaho; plants 10-61 cm tall, 20-30 cm across); first seed and lifespan estimated from bunchgrass habit

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds germinate with autumn or early-spring moisture into a tiny tuft of soft, fine, folded blue-green leaves with boat-shaped tips. It grows through the cool season and forms a small, dense bunch of basal leaves (a few cm up to 30 cm across) with slender culms bearing narrow, often purplish panicles; it cures straw-coloured and goes dormant by early summer.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Poa secunda (50% germination after 3 months after-ripening; Idaho: stalks late April, flowering early June, seed ripe late June, shed June-July; bunches from 1-2 culms to 30 cm across; relatively short-lived; open sun to partial shade, shaded out by sagebrush). Growth rate and lifespan estimated.
